title: Work–Energy Theorem & Conservation of Energy
theory: $W = Fd\cos\phi$; net work $= \Delta KE$. With only conservative forces, $E = KE + PE$ is constant; friction drains $f \times d_{rel}$ as heat; ideal tensions and normal forces do no net work. Two-body recoil systems (a spring between free masses) need **energy and momentum together**: momentum fixes the speed *ratio*, energy fixes the *scale*. Maximum-speed moments occur where acceleration is zero — for springs, at natural length.
framework: Is momentum conserved (no external horizontal force)?
Is mechanical energy conserved (no friction, no sticking)?
Identify *where* the asked extremum happens (usually natural length / lowest point).

problems.title: Two masses released with a stretched spring

parts.parameters:
- Given: masses $M$ and $m$ on a frictionless horizontal table, joined by a spring of constant $k$; released from rest with stretch $\ell$.
- Find: maximum speed of $m$.
- Diagram: M —spring— m on a line; both fly apart as the spring relaxes.
parts.formulas: momentum $0 = Mv_M - mv_m$; energy $\frac{1}{2}k\ell^2 = \frac{1}{2}Mv_M^2 + \frac{1}{2}mv_m^2$; speeds peak at natural length.
parts.conclusion: the speeds peak exactly when the spring crosses natural length (force, hence acceleration, flips sign there). Limit $M\to\infty$ recovers the fixed-wall result $\sqrt{k\ell^2/m}$ ✓ — that single limit eliminates four of the six options.
